podcast.title: The purple scarf

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: Have you ever made something by hand? Guess: what did Sam make at a workshop?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is crafts and handmade things. And look what I'm wearing!
The scarf! My grandmother finished it?
Last night. She gave it to me with a glass of tea. It's purple and very, very warm.
She worked on it for a month. For her, it's a labour of love.
I can see it. Every row is perfect. How does she do it?
Seventy years of practice. And patience. She learned to knit when she was nine.
Well, I tried something new too. A pottery workshop near Fountain Square.
Pottery! What did you make?
A bowl. Well — it's supposed to be a bowl. It's a bit… imperfect. [laugh]
Imperfect is the beauty of handmade things. Every one is different.
That is what the teacher said. She says it takes a year to learn the ropes.
Have you seen the carpet makers in the Old City?
Yes! A woman was weaving a carpet by hand. The pattern was so detailed.
Some carpets take a whole year. My family has one that's a hundred years old.
A hundred years! Things like that are made to last.
Not like the cheap carpets from big shops. They're finished in two years.
And there is the copper village, Lahij. Is it true every house is a workshop?
Almost. You can hear the hammers in the whole street. It's a real craft village — you should go.
Next month. And I'll bring my bowl to show them. [chuckle]
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: have you ever made something by hand — and what is the most special handmade thing you own?
Mine is this scarf, of course. See you next time!
Bye for now!
